extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO (trademark attorneys and non-registered practitioners); USPTO OED staff; attorneys interested in professional conduct rules
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO OED Final Order setting out stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions for professional misconduct by a practitioner in trademark matters before the USPTO (TTAB). Includes cited USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) — keep client reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of violations in this case: not informing the client that the practitioner filed a notice of withdrawal in the TTAB cancellation proceeding; not informing the client that the LAYSA trademark registration was cancelled; and filing a second trademark application for the client while knowing the client had no actual knowledge of that filing. The Final Order treats failure to keep the client reasonably informed as actionable misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(4) — promptly comply with reasonable requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: failing to respond to multiple reasonable requests for status, information, and invoices sent by the client and the client's foreign (Colombian) attorney/assistant over many months. The Order cites failure to respond as a violation of this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.303(a)(3) — do not offer evidence practitioner knows to be false
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes a practitioner from knowingly offering evidence that the practitioner knows to be false and requires remedial measures (37 C.F.R. §11.303(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter, the rule is applied to conduct including forging an electronic signature on a motion and filing a motion containing false representations. The Order cites this provision as violated by the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.304(b) — do not falsify evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes a practitioner from falsifying evidence (37 C.F.R. §11.304(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order treats forging the electronic signature of a foreign attorney on a TTAB motion as falsifying evidence and cites §11.304(b) as violated. The document references electronic signature requirements elsewhere (37 C.F.R. §2.193(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.303(a)(1) — do not knowingly make false statements to a tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes a practitioner from knowingly making a false statement of fact or law to a tribunal (37 C.F.R. §11.303(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied here to the respondent's knowing false representations to the TTAB when requesting permission to withdraw (e.g., falsely stating the client had been notified, that papers had been handed over, that the client had engaged new counsel, and that the client requested additional time). The Order cites this rule as violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — no conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. §11.804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites this provision in connection with the respondent's forged signature and false tribunal representations, treating such conduct as prohibited professional misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — no conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. §11.804(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites this provision for the respondent's false statements to the TTAB and related conduct that undermined the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 2.193(c) — electronic signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic signature requirements for filings before the USPTO (37 C.F.R. §2.193(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnoted in the Order: the respondent forged the electronic signature of a foreign attorney not authorized to practice before the USPTO. The rule is cited to show the filing/signature requirements that were violated by forging a signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional authority: 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director and the Office of Enrollment and Discipline have jurisdiction to impose discipline under 35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and applicable regulations (37 C.F.R. §§11.19 and 11.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states the statutory and regulatory basis for the Director's authority to approve settlement agreements and enter disciplinary Final Orders. This establishes the procedural framework for evaluating and sanctioning practitioner misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 — compliance with suspension terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements relating to suspension from practice before the Office; respondent 'shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58' as part of the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order imposes a 12-month suspension from practice before the Office in trademark and non-patent matters and requires the respondent's compliance with the suspension regulation. This is presented as the agreed-upon sanction and its regulatory compliance obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 — publication of disciplinary order
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory provision governing publication of disciplinary orders; the OED Director 'shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.59'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires the OED Director to publish the Final Order and to post it in the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette, consistent with §11.59's publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for reinstatement — CLE in ethics law and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition for reinstatement after suspension, the respondent must complete at least twelve (12) hours of continuing legal education (CLE) in the field of ethics law and submit proof of completion as part of any reinstatement petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express requirement of the Final Order tied to reinstatement; it functions as a remedial/rehabilitative criterion the respondent must satisfy to resume practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to communicate/or avoid misrepresentations when withdrawing
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not misrepresent to a tribunal or others about the status of client notification, transfer of papers, or the client's engagement of new counsel when filing motions to withdraw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists specific misrepresentations in the respondent's Motion to Withdraw (that he had notified the client, turned over papers, that the client had engaged new counsel, and that the client requested additional time) and treats those misrepresentations as violations of the Rules (e.g., §11.303(a)(1), §11.804). This entry highlights withdrawal-related communication duties evidenced by the case facts.
